item.title: How international aid groups are dealing with the pain of slashed USAID funding
item.description: Trump’s dismantling of USAID and deep foreign aid cuts are forcing international NGOs to shrink, localise and seek new funding models – with profound consequences for global health and humanitarian work.

item.title: As climate diplomacy stalls, the economics are racing ahead
item.description: Despite political gridlock within countries and at global summits, climate change and ecological degradation are creating undeniable economic momentum. As renewables scale up, fossil fuels will become even less competitive; and as ecosystems degrade, markets will price in the risks and reward those who adapt.

item.title: Dr Hezri Adnan joins UNDP Malaysia as senior advisor on sustainable development
item.description: He was previously group sustainability director at stock exchange Bursa Malaysia, where he has been succeeded by Dr Ken Yeoh Kyid.

item.title: How to improve Chinese farmers’ resilience to climate change
item.description: Creating good policies requires better data gathering and a fairer allocation of resources, otherwise farmers bear all the risks.

item.title: Singapore offers grants to drinks producers to offset polluter-pays scheme costs
item.description: But some producers question whether the S$2,500 grant will be sufficient to offset the costs of the scheme, which a minister said on Tuesday would not be subject to further delays and go live on 1 April.

item.title: East Asia seas hit near-record heat as global oceans store more warmth
item.description: Sea surface temperatures in waters around South Korea and across East Asia hit some of their highest levels on record last year, accelerating climate risks to marine ecosystems and the country's fisheries, government data showed.

item.title: Aceh’s bitter lesson, relearned
item.description: In 2004, Aceh was hardest hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami. In 2025, Indonesia’s most disaster-aware province was among the worst hit by floods. The failure was not forecasting, but what happened – or didn’t – after the alarms were raised.

item.title: How to feed ten billion people
item.description: With the world’s population expected to reach ten billion by mid-century, agriculture must produce more with less – every season, everywhere. The knowledge and tools to end and prevent food insecurity are already in hand, but they have yet to be used wisely and at scale.

item.title: Asylum seekers brace for bleak 2026 as countries clamp down
item.description: Protections shrink for refugees and asylum seekers as leaders from Donald Trump in the US to Britain's Keir Starmer toughen rules.

item.title: Adopting low-cost ‘healthy’ diets could cut food emissions by one-third
item.description: Choosing the “least expensive” healthy food options could cut dietary emissions by one-third, according to a recent study.
